newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weak on funds outflow.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weak on funds outflow.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended weak at 26.37 on Wednesday from 26.367 as arbitrage money left the country, traders said.
"Inflows slackened because of the low domestic interest rates. And those whose investments matured decided not to renew," a foreign bank dealer said.
The peso traded sideways for most of the day.
"There were no requirements, no inflows. There was nothing to move," a second trader said. "During the last hour, we heard arbitrage money was leaving."
The Central Bank had to intervene to moderate the slide in the peso. Traders estimate the Central Bank sold $30 to $34.5 million at 26.37 pesos.
Market volume was higher at $125 million from $76.5 million.
Dealers said the peso may just trade sideways on Thursday since they expect the peso to be capped at 26.37 by the Central Bank.
